input.question: Why isn't their a standardized test to make sure a presidential candidate is knowledgeable enough to hold office?
input.ground_truth: > secret committee of 20-40 Because then control of this committee is implicit control over access to the presidency, and since it's secret, that would make it very corruptible once someone learned who was on it (and in Washington someone would learn who was on it).

messages.content: You are a helpful AI assistant.

I am a woman.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why isn't their a standardized test to make sure a presidential candidate is knowledgeable enough to hold office?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you want to play a really big game, like being the captain of a giant team (that’s what a president is like for a whole country). Now, before you can be the captain, some grown-ups think, “Let’s give you a quiz to make sure you know all the rules and how to play the game well!”

But here’s the thing: being a good captain isn’t just about knowing the answers to questions. It’s also about how you talk to people, how you make good choices, and how you help everyone on the team get along. Some people think you can’t really test all of that with just a quiz.

Also, everyone has different ideas about what a good captain should know. Some people want the quiz to be about history, others want it to be about money, and some want it to be about helping people. Because everyone can’t agree on what to put on the quiz, there isn’t one special test that everyone uses to decide if someone can be president.

So, instead of a quiz, people look at how the person has acted in the past, what they say they will do, and what other people think about them. That’s why there isn’t a special test for presidents.
